answer: Require a fresh memory-hard puzzle per identity each epoch. The registry publishes a random beacon; an agent hashes its public key with it using Argon2 at 2 GB memory until the output beats a difficulty target. Verifiers recheck with one hash. Nothing can be precomputed or shared, so a tundra of dormant fakes lapses unless it keeps paying. An orchard of one hundred keys needs a hundred cores and RAM slices, about eight dollars monthly for each jade-cheap clone.
